title: still present since round 3: send_reminder / remind_applicant / send_bulk_invite mutate nothing and return canned counts that contradict the seeded awaiting list
detail: Store functions now return the store unchanged plus hardcoded counts; demo_api still discards 'next'. The canned (2,1) contradicts the r4-derived remindable_count=1/followup_count=1, and the awaiting list never reflects a sent reminder.
recommended_fix: Parse the submitted emails, flip reminded/followed_up on static_awaiting rows, compute the result counts from the actual mutation, and thread the mutated store.

title: still present since round 3: vacancy/status mutations return Ok unconditionally - nonexistent ids report success; the Result error channel is dead
evidence: '#(DemoStore(..store, vacancies: updated), Ok(vacancy_id))' (archive_vacancy, restore_vacancy, close_vacancy) and '#(DemoStore(..store, vacancies: updated), Ok(slug))' (change_status)
detail: The list.map no-ops when no vacancy/application matches yet Ok is returned; callers cannot distinguish a miss from a mutation, so the demo reports success for ids that do not exist.
recommended_fix: Check the match after the map and return Error on miss, or drop the Result and simplify the call chain.

title: still present since round 3: mark_opened doc claims an idempotent Submitted->UnderReview transition but applies it to any status
detail: No status guard in the store: mark_opened transitions an application of ANY status (e.g. Approved) to UnderReview and appends an audit entry; idempotency rests entirely on the dispatch-layer open_dispatched set.
recommended_fix: Transition only when the current status is Submitted; otherwise leave the store unchanged.

title: still present since round 3: create_vacancy derives the id from an 8-char-truncated name slug with no uniqueness check
detail: Two demo-created vacancies whose property names share an 8-char cleaned prefix (and the same short_code 'RTDEMO'<>suffix) collide; the second silently overwrites the first in store lookups.
recommended_fix: Append a disambiguator (sequence or vacancy count) or extend the suffix until unique within the store.

title: r3 B4 fix partial: refcheck pins landed at store level only - the demo_update refcheck threading arms (and single mark-read) still have no dispatch-level pin
evidence:
demo_flow_test.gleam: 'let #(after_skip, _) =
    demo_store.refcheck_action(
      store,
      "v-maples",
      "a-tom",
      "rc-tom-employer",
      "skip",
    )' (calls demo_store directly). grep over client/test/demo/ for UserChoseRefcheckAction/UserSavedRefcheckEdit/UserConfirmedRefcheckAction/UserClickedNotification returns NONE - the only dispatch-level refcheck tests are real-path tests in client_test.gleam:6402-6723.
detail: The r4 claim was 'refcheck dispatch pins'; the landed pins bypass client.update, so reverting fire_demo_refcheck's 'demo_store: Some(next)' threading (the r2-B5 regression class) stays green. Mutation logic itself is pinned at store level.
recommended_fix: Add one dispatch-level test per refcheck arm (client.update with UserChoseRefcheckAction skip / UserSavedRefcheckEdit substitute) asserting the store on the model changed.

title: still present since round 3 (partially): download_timeout still duplicated between client.gleam and demo_update.gleam with divergent signatures (store_of half is fixed)
detail: Two download_timeout variants persist with different arities (one hardcodes 90_000); the r3 note covered both helper pairs and only store_of was lifted.
recommended_fix: Lift download_timeout into a shared demo helper (or call client.gleam's two-arg variant) and delete the duplicate.

title: still present since round 3: demo_not_in_demo_toast diverges from add_toast's id convention - ids can collide and one timeout dismisses both
evidence: demo_update.gleam: 'let toast_id = model.next_toast_id + 1' then 'next_toast_id: toast_id'; client.gleam add_toast: 'let id = model.next_toast_id' then '#(Model(..model, toasts: capped_toasts, next_toast_id: id + 1), dismiss_eff)'
detail: Sequence verified: add_toast (id=N, next=N+1) -> demo toast (id=N+2, next=N+2) -> next add_toast uses id=N+2, colliding with the outstanding demo toast; a single AppDismissToast(N+2) dismisses both.
recommended_fix: Reuse add_toast (or its id allocation) for the demo info toasts.

title: still present since round 3: status_from_slug silently coerces any unknown status slug to Submitted
detail: A typo in any demo action wire silently lands as Submitted instead of failing loudly.
recommended_fix: Return a Result or panic on unknown slugs in the demo store.

title: still present since round 3: report_download_test pins the id mapping but not baked-asset presence - a deleted or misnamed PDF 404s silently
evidence: The file contains only analysis_id_maps_to_baked_key_test and every_baked_report_has_a_matching_analysis_test (id-mapping assertions like 'demo_api.application_id_from_analysis("an-aoife") |> should.equal("a-aoife")'); no test reads server/priv/static/demo/.
detail: The mapping is pinned but the existence of the baked PDFs on disk is not; a missing asset only surfaces as a demo download failure.
recommended_fix: Assert every report_filenames entry has a baked asset on disk (build-time check).

title: still present since round 3: demo_flow_test header claims bug-hunt E2E coverage that does not exist; demo_requests_are_intercepted_test cannot distinguish demo from real dispatch
evidence: Header: '//// resolves it. The browser E2E (bug-hunt) covers the effect execution.' - but ls .pi/skills/bug-hunt/scenarios/ shows analytics/applications/auth/billing/comparison/dashboard/errors/landing/notifications/settings (no demo scenario; grep for 'demo' matches only seed workflows). demo_requests_are_intercepted_test asserts only 'Loading -> Nil' transitions, which pass identically if the real arm runs and fails.
